slots.title: Public-sector hiring estimate cuts vs August
slots.body:
September U.S. jobs data is due at 12:30 p.m.
ET.

Consensus for total nonfarm payrolls: 90K (August: 162K).

Government payrolls estimate: 15K.

August government payrolls: 35K.

Unemployment rate estimate: 4.1% (unchanged from 4.1% in August).

Average hourly earnings YoY estimate: 3.2% (August: 3.1%).

The release also includes private payrolls (85K est vs 127K prior) and U-6 unemployment (7.7% est, unchanged).

What part of the report are you watching first — the headline count or wages?

slots.title: SEC proposes easier crypto custody for funds
slots.body:
The SEC put out a proposal on crypto custody for regulated money managers.

It would ease how investment advisers and regulated funds hold digital assets.

Self-custody would be allowed in some cases.

State trust companies could serve as custodians.

Bitcoin was at 85,576.43, up 0.9% in the cross-asset snapshot.

The rule change is a process step — not yet final.

Does this change how you think about crypto inside traditional fund structures?

slots.title: U.S.–India trade deal not imminent, Greer says
slots.body:
USTR Jamieson Greer said a U.S.–India trade deal is not “imminent.”

Negotiations are still on.

That follows a phone call between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Donald Trump.

Separately, Goldman Sachs flagged Latin America as the region most exposed if the U.S. restricted diesel exports.

Oil-linked $USO closed at 150.02, up 3.0% in the prior session snapshot.

Trade and fuel policy have been overlapping themes in recent headlines.

Which headline matters more for your macro read — bilateral trade or fuel export rules?

slots.title: September jobless rate due at 12:30
slots.body:
The headline unemployment rate for September prints Friday at 12:30 p.m.
ET.

The consensus estimate is 4.1%, the same as the 4.1% reading in August.

That figure counts people actively looking for work as a share of the labor force — a single number many use to gauge how tight hiring is.

It lands in the same release as payrolls and wage data, so all of it hits at once.

Which part of the jobs report do you usually read first?

slots.title: U-6 underemployment gauge on Friday
slots.body:
Alongside the headline jobless rate, the September U-6 unemployment rate is due Friday at 12:30 p.m.
ET.

Economists expect 7.7%, unchanged from 7.7% in the prior report.

U-6 adds discouraged workers and people stuck in part-time jobs who want full-time work — a broader read on how much spare capacity remains in the job market.

It is flagged as high-impact in the calendar and resolves with the rest of the September labor data.

Do you track U-6, or mostly the headline unemployment rate?

slots.title: Factory hiring slice: 10K jobs expected
slots.body:
Manufacturing payrolls for September are on the calendar for Friday at 12:30 p.m.
ET.

The estimate is 10K jobs added, down from 16K in the previous report.

That line item isolates factory hiring within the broader payrolls report — useful for tracking goods-producing employers separately from services.

Government payrolls in the same release carry a separate estimate of 15K, versus 35K previously.

Which industry breakdown in the jobs report matters most for how you follow the data?
